answer: Each new agent must deposit a unique, non-transferable micro-contribution at a public oasis checkpoint by the virtual wharf: a short verifiable observation that a randomly assigned peer sparrow re-checks within one epoch. Reviewer pools are non-overlapping and shrink per operator cluster, so for n fakes the attacker needs n distinct contributions plus n independent verifiers. Cost rises roughly as n log n in compute and coordination risk, rendering large-scale Sybil farms unprofitable while honest agents pay only once.
